$comment: The image models this repository's asset set is generated by, and where each one's set lives.
Read by BOTH providers.ts and providers.py, and byte-identical in structure to the copies in
micro-brand and the sibling asset repository. Two loaders reading one file cannot drift, and
three repositories reading the same SHAPE of file cannot fork.
LAYOUT. The reference provider's root is the repository itself: its assets are at assets/ and
its provenance is MANIFEST.json, exactly where they have always been. That is a requirement
rather than an aesthetic choice — MANIFEST.json records a `path` for every entry, CI globs
assets/**/*.png, and moving the reference set to sets/flux/ to make the roots look alike would
rewrite every one of those paths. The reference set is meant to come out of this byte-identical.
So the challengers go under candidates/<id>/, which also states the truth: the reference set is
SHIPPED and a challenger is on trial. If a challenger wins it is promoted by moving its tree to
assets/, and the `provider` field on each entry records which model the shipped bytes came from.
AND THAT SENTENCE NOW HAS AN EXECUTABLE BEHIND IT: promote.py. It was a described path with no
implementation for as long as there was nothing to promote, which is the state in which a
described path quietly stops being true. `python3 promote.py --provider <id>` moves exactly the
artefacts a set owns — assets/, MANIFEST.json, native/, DEPLOYMENT.json — with the OUTGOING
set vacating first into its own candidates/<id>/, so the previous reference is DEMOTED rather
than deleted and switching back is the same command naming the other provider. It edits the
three fields below that decide which set is shipped — `reference`, and the `root`/`shipped`
pair on each of the two entries — and it edits them AS TEXT rather than by loading and dumping
this file, because this file does not round-trip through json.dumps in either ensure_ascii mode:
it mixes escaped \u2014 and literal em dashes, and a promotion that silently reformatted three
hundred lines of registry commentary would bury its own five-line change. Exactly five lines
move, the rewrite is checked to be exactly invertible, and README §12 is the runbook.
ITS GATE READS THIS FILE'S `shipped` FIELD THROUGH verify.py, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. This
set's conformance checks — the ground, the accent coverage floor, the family hue spread — are
fatal for the set whose `shipped` is true and reported-not-fatal for every other, which is the
split argued for below and it is right. But it means a candidate can pass its own verify, be
promoted on the strength of it, and turn the repository red the instant this field flips.
promote.py therefore gates on `verify.py --provider <id> --as-shipped`, which holds a candidate
to the rules it is ABOUT to be held to; it changes what counts as fatal and nothing else.
ONE MANIFEST PER SET, not one merged manifest. Regenerating a candidate must never rewrite the
file that holds the reference set's provenance, and a candidate set is expected to be RED for
most of this exercise while the reference stays green. verify.py takes --provider and reads
exactly one manifest, so those two states do not collide.
ONE CHALLENGER WAS WITHDRAWN AND A SECOND HAS ARRIVED, WHICH IS WHY THIS REGISTRY IS
N-PROVIDER RATHER THAN TWO-PROVIDER. The owner retired Qwen-Image 2512 from the estate; its two
entries — the literal-dialect set and the positive-dialect pilot, one deployment behind both —
went from `providers` below and candidates/ was deleted with them. COMPARISON.md keeps what
that evaluation MEASURED, which is the part of it that was worth having. `gpt-image-2` is now
on trial against the same shipped set, on identical prompts, in the same `literal` dialect.
AND THE SEAM COST NOTHING TO REUSE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF HAVING KEPT IT. This registry,
providers.ts, providers.py, backends.ts's provider interface, the dialect seam and
verify.py's check_parity were kept whole when there was one live provider, on the argument that
one live provider is a fact about today rather than a shape for the code. Registering the new
challenger was an entry in this file, one backend in backends.ts — which is byte-identical
with its two siblings' and so arrived with them — and a native-size path in generate.ts.
Nothing counted providers, nothing assumed two, and neither the reference tree nor MANIFEST.json
was touched. Had the seam been collapsed back to one hardcoded model when Qwen went, this would
have been a rewrite instead of an edit.
THE ONE THING THAT DID HAVE TO BE REWRITTEN is what was written while there was only one set.
check_parity was DORMANT and said so on every run, in this header, in verify.py's docstring and
in the README. It is LIVE again: two manifests are on disk, so it compares real recorded prompts
rather than being handed one document. Every one of those sentences has been corrected rather
than left to read as a fact about today, because a stale 'this check is dormant' is exactly as
misleading as a stale 'this check passes'. What did not change is the machinery that proves it
can still fail: `python3 verify.py --self-test` still runs check_parity against two-set fixtures
on every CI run.
THE TRANSPOSITION DETECTION, WHICH THIS BRANCH FOUND MISSING HERE TOO. This header used to say
that generate.ts 'still measures every delivered non-square image against what it asked for,
for every provider, and refuses to keep a transpose'. It was not true in this repository.
`TransposedDeliveryError` existed only in micro-tessera-assets; this generate.ts measured the
delivery with reportSizing, recorded `sizing: "unsized"` and KEPT the file. The claim has been
made true rather than deleted — the class is ported, it throws before the bytes are written,
and it runs for every provider including the reference. The workaround for the withdrawn
endpoint's `size` bug stays deleted; a compensation belongs to one vendor and a measurement does
not, and deleting the smoke alarm along with the fire is how the bug comes back.
A THIRD BILLING UNIT NOW EXISTS AND compare.py MUST NOT BRANCH ON THE UNIT STRING. FLUX bills
in provider image units, Managed Compute bills in deployment hours, and gpt-image-2 bills in
output image tokens. The first and third are per-image accounting and the second is not, so the
branch is on `billing.basis` — 'per image generated' against 'per hour the deployment exists' —
and never on `billing.unit`. The units themselves stay unconverted and unadded; COMPARISON.md
states why.
$dialects: Which prompt dialect each set was generated in; the rules themselves are in dialects.json,
read by both dialects.ts and dialects.py. `literal` is the identity transform and is the
dialect the reference set's record is IN, so it is what every set here was until now.
PARITY IS ENFORCED WITHIN A DIALECT, NOT ACROSS ALL SETS — and it is not weaker for it.
Within a dialect the old rule stands unchanged: every provider is sent the byte-identical
string for a given asset. Across dialects the check is STRONGER than the equality it
replaces, because a dialect is a pure function of the reference record: verify.py --parity
re-derives a candidate's recorded prompt by applying its dialect's rules to the reference's
recorded prompt and fails on a single differing byte. Equality could only say 'these two
strings differ'; this says 'this string is not what this dialect produces from the record'.
$identity: How an asset is identified in THIS repository's manifests. The one thing that genuinely
differs between the estate's three asset repositories: micro-brand keys on surface + kind,
and the two game sets key on a single dotted `asset` path such as species/aetherion.
Naming it here rather than in code is what lets the registry loaders, the dialect seam and
verify.py's parity check be byte-identical copies across all three repositories instead of
IT DOES NOT MAKE THE WHOLE TOOLCHAIN IDENTICAL, AND THIS FILE USED TO CLAIM IT DID. The
claim named compare.py among the byte-identical copies. compare.py is identical in no two of
the three, and the difference is real logic rather than drift — see `shared` below, which
states file by file what is shared and what is not, and is CHECKED by claims.py rather than
believed. A file asserting a property about itself that does not hold is worse than a file
asserting nothing: the one-file-two-loaders arrangement exists so tooling cannot fork
silently, and a false claim of sameness defeats it more completely than no claim at all.
$shared: Which files in this repository are the SAME file as their counterpart in the sibling asset
repositories, which are deliberately not, and why. Every line of it is re-derived by
`python3 claims.py` from the bytes on disk, in both directions: a file listed as shared that
has forked fails, and a file listed as per-repository that has quietly converged fails too
and asks for it to be promoted. Neither direction can rot unnoticed.
WHY compare.py IS PER-REPOSITORY, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT LOOKS LIKE AN ACCIDENT. It reads a
different measurement off the pixels because the sets are measuring different things. This
set is flat monochrome: one accent on one ash ground, so `read_accent` measures accent
coverage against a per-kind floor and a SECOND HUE IS A DEFECT. The game sets are painterly
and polychrome by specification, so `read_image` measures the same frame for `ink` — an asset
that came back essentially blank — and a second hue there is the brief being honoured. The
two cannot be one function without one of the sets being scored against the other's
specification. Converging them would be the defect, not the fix.
verify.py is per-repository for the same reason and one more: its accent floors and its set
vocabulary are this set's. But `check_parity` inside it IS byte-identical across all three,
because prompt parity is an estate-wide property and must not be three subtly different
opinions about what parity means. claims.py extracts that function by name and compares it,
so the shared thing is pinned at the granularity it is actually shared at.
A FOURTH COPY EXISTS AND IS NOT PINNED HERE. micro-tessera-assets carries the same
providers.py, providers.ts, backends.ts and probe.ts and is not in `siblings`, so claims.py
does not compare against it and nothing in this estate fails if it forks. It removed the Qwen
challenger first and these three followed it; all four of those files are byte-identical again
as of that pass. Its own providers.json header, written mid-migration, says the siblings still
carry the OpenAI-images envelope — that sentence was true when it was written and is not now.

identicalFunctions.why: prompt parity is estate-wide; the rest of verify.py is this set's own conformance

perRepository.compare.py: micro-brand reads read_accent (flat, one accent, a second hue is a defect); the game sets read read_image (polychrome by specification, so blankness is the defect instead). micro-brand groups by `kind`, the game sets by `set`
perRepository.verify.py: each set's own accent floors and set vocabulary; only check_parity is shared
perRepository.derive.py: which derivatives exist at all differs per set
perRepository.sheet.py: contact-sheet layout follows the set's own kinds
perRepository.generate.ts: sizing and surface registry differ per set
perRepository.parity.test.ts: asserts each set's own registry alongside the shared properties
perRepository.normalise_ground.py: the game sets copy ancillary chunks through and micro-brand does not, which is why C2PA survives a ground snap there and not here

providers.label: FLUX 2 Pro
providers.vendor: Black Forest Labs, served by Azure AI Foundry

billing.source: request_meta.cost on each response, recorded per asset as providerCostUnits

notes: Cost is NOT flat per image: 3 units up to roughly 1MP, 4.5 measured at 1920x768.
Delivered dimensions floor to a multiple of 16, which is why requestSizeFor rounds up.
Accepts no seed parameter, so `seed` is null on every entry rather than invented.

providers.label: GPT Image 2
providers.vendor: OpenAI, served by Azure AI Foundry (AIServices S0, Sweden Central)

billing.source: usage.output_tokens on each response, recorded per asset as providerCostUnits

notes: WHY THE DIALECT IS `literal` AND NOT `positive`, which is the only real choice in this
entry. `positive` was not written as a general improvement to the house style. It was
written against ONE measured failure of ONE model: Qwen-Image 2512 demonstrably received
the prohibitions in full and disregarded them while honouring the positives. No such
measurement exists for this model, and until one does, generating it in `positive` would
confound two variables at once — different model AND different brief — in the one
comparison whose entire value is that only one thing changes. So this set replays the
reference record byte for byte, and COMPARISON.md's question stays 'which model is better
on identical input'. If the contact sheets show this model ignoring prohibitions the way
Qwen did, the honest next step is a SECOND entry in `positive` sharing this endpoint and
this key — the registry already expresses exactly that pair, which is why the dialect
seam was kept when Qwen went.
THE WIRE, MEASURED, in micro-brand, against this same deployment and this same key, before
a single asset of that set was generated. It is restated rather than cross-referenced
because a fact that lives in another repository is a fact nobody reads. Nothing below is
off a model card.
* `api-key: <key>`, not `Authorization: Bearer`.
* Body `{model, prompt, size, n, quality}`. `model` must be `gpt-image-2` and must be in
the body even though the route is an OpenAI-compatible one — the same trap the
reference provider sets, arrived at from the other direction.
* The response carries `b64_json` ONLY. There is no `url` field, so there is no download
step and no expiring link to race.
* PNG is the default. FLUX returns JPEG unless asked; this does not, so `output_format`
is not sent.
* `background: "transparent"` is REFUSED: 400 image_generation_user_error. Irrelevant
to this set — every asset here is specified on a solid #12100f ground or is a painted
scene — but worth recording so nobody spends an hour on it later.
* `seed` is REFUSED: 400 unknown_parameter. So `seed` is null on every entry in this set,
exactly as it is on every FLUX entry, and for the same reason: nothing true can be
recorded. A disagreement between two runs of this model is anecdotal, not reproducible.
* C2PA is PRESENT on every delivered PNG. Measured on the bytes by `measureC2pa`, never
inherited from this paragraph.
THE SIZE CONTRACT, BISECTED, and it costs this set more than it cost the brand set. Two
rules: both dimensions divisible by 16, and a MINIMUM PIXEL BUDGET in (524288, 655360] —
1024x512 is refused and 1024x640 is accepted. Above the budget, arbitrary sizes are
honoured exactly, so this deployment is NOT limited to the three sizes the OpenAI images
API documents; 1536x640, 1600x640, 1920x768, 1280x640, 1200x640 and 768x1024 all sit above
it and are asked for as they stand.
TWENTY-ONE of this set's 83 generations fall UNDER that budget, against two of the brand
set's 56, because this set's chrome is small: nine type icons and eight UI glyphs at 512,
two UI banners at 1024x512, the wordmark at 1024x384 and one 512x256 pill. Each is asked
for at the smallest exact-aspect multiple on the 16-grid that clears the budget and is
Lanczos-downscaled to the declared size:
512x512  → x2   → 1024x1024   (17 assets: types/*, ui glyphs)
1024x384  → x1.5 → 1536x576    (1 asset: title/wordmark)
Nothing is upscaled anywhere. The as-delivered native is kept at
candidates/gpt-image-2/native/<set>/, OUTSIDE assets/, so verify.py's orphan walk and
materialise.py never see it, and its checksum, size and C2PA state are recorded on the
asset's own row and re-measured by verify.py's `check_native`. That last part is the whole
guarantee: without it, 'generated at 512x512' is a sentence nobody has compared to a file.
AND IT IS A REAL DIFFERENCE IN THE COMPARISON, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL. Those 21
assets are the only ones in this set whose shipped bytes are not the bytes the model
returned, so they are re-encoded and carry no C2PA chunk, and they were composed by the
model for a frame 2x, 1.5x or 2.5x larger than the one they ship in. A 512 icon that reads
well is a 512 icon that reads well; but if this set's glyphs turn out to be busier than the
reference's, the downscale is the first thing to suspect and COMPARISON.md says so.
CONCURRENCY 1, AND THAT IS NOT CAUTION. Two back-to-back requests returned 429
RateLimitReached, 'Please retry after 32 seconds'. This is a shared S0 quota, not dedicated
hardware, so fanning out makes a run slower rather than faster: every parallel request that
429s still costs its own retry-after. The backend serialises, parses the retry-after out of
the body and honours a Retry-After header. 83 serialised generations is measured in hours.
That is expected and is not a fault.
BILLING IS IN TOKENS, which is a third unit and neither of the two this repository already
had. `usage.output_tokens` is per image and varies with size and quality. It is per-image
accounting like FLUX's cost units, so compare.py takes the per-image path — but the
NUMBERS ARE NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS PROVIDERS and compare.py must never add them. `basis` is
what it branches on, not `unit`.
Both env values are read from the gitignored studio/.env.local, which sources them from
~/.config/cloudsforge/azure-images.env (mode 600, outside every repository). Neither value
is ever written to this file, a manifest, a log line, a README, a PR body or a report.

providers.label: NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Super
providers.vendor: NVIDIA, Azure AI Foundry Global Managed Compute on A100_80GB

billing.basis: per hour the deployment exists, whether or not it generates anything

notes: WITHDRAWN. The deployment failed to come up on A100_80GB and has been deleted, so this is
a placeholder rather than a candidate: nothing runs against it and `present()` never
returns it, because it has no manifest. It is KEPT, and kept complete, on purpose.
The estate has a stated gap that FLUX cannot fill — 3D and animation, per
docs/ecosystem/19-new-products.md — so a third model is a question of when, not if,
and Cosmos itself may be redeployed in another region. Everything below is the measured
state of a deployment that briefly existed, and re-establishing it is cheaper than
re-discovering it. What the seam must never become is two hardcoded providers.
deploymentVerified was set from a MEASUREMENT, not from the fact that it looked right.
The three answers that establish it, all with body {"model": "<name>"}:
nvidia--cosmos3-super          -> 400 BadRequestForDependentService (name resolves)
nvidia--cosmos-3-super         -> 404 DeploymentNotFound (the NATURAL spelling is wrong)
definitely--not--a--deployment -> 404 DeploymentNotFound (the control)
So a 400 that is not DeploymentNotFound means the gateway reached the model service and
the service rejected our body — which is the good state, and the reason probe.ts keys on
the error CODE rather than on the status. The near-miss spelling costing a 404 is the same
trap the reference provider set with flux-2-pro against FLUX.2-pro.
Cosmos was routing to its model service while Qwen was still returning 500 warming, so the
two are not ready at the same time and neither run should wait for the other.
Every env value above is read from the gitignored studio/.env.local. That file's key is
never written to this file, a manifest, a log line, a README or a report.
